function: Learned real-time beam-to-cell allocation (MFMAPPO) for LEO satellites under uneven traffic and jamming; potential-game statistical beams and fractional-programming power allocation are not learned (pp. 7-9).
system: Three LEO satellites at 1000 km, 8 beams each, 100 cells, 20 GHz Ka-band, 50 MHz bandwidth, no RIS (p. 10, Table I).
method: Multiagent PPO with mean-field approximation (MFMAPPO), centralized training and decentralized execution, MLP actor and critic, 5000 training episodes; hybrid with game-theoretic planning and fractional programming (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom link-budget simulator: free-space loss, ITU-R S.1528 and S.465-6 antenna patterns, log-normal rain attenuation (ITU-R P.1853), fixed jamming power, Poisson traffic 50-500 Mb/s; no dataset (pp. 4, 10, 14).
test_conditions: 5000 training episodes of 100 slots; tests on 100 random traffic instances at 10 Gb/s, three jamming levels, demands 10-30 Gb/s, 10% missing inputs (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: Random, Periodic, Greedy, genetic algorithm; learned: independent multiagent DQN (IQL), MAPPO, and MFMAPPO without statistical planning (pp. 10-13).
metrics: Throughput or demand satisfaction (Gb/s), throughput CDF, normalized reward convergence, training and execution time (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Orders: O(K^2 N) statistical planning, O(T n^2) training, O(n) inference, O(K^3 log(1/xi)) power; runtime 977 us versus 1576 us all-real-time (pp. 9, 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "According to ITU-R S.465-6 [33], the" earth station antenna model, with the satellite antenna per ITU-R S.1528 [32] and rain attenuation [34] (ITU-R P.1853, p. 14) in the link gain; standardized ITU-R models, not 3GPP.
q2_support: p. 12: "Then, we tested 100 randomly generated traffic instances" under the same total demand and jamming; the jamming-level, demand and 10% missing-input tests (pp. 12-13) are sweeps, and the paper never states that training used different conditions.
q3_support: p. 12: "achieves higher throughput compared to the benchmark algorithms, including GA, Greedy, IQL, and Periodic Service." GA, Greedy, Random and Periodic are non-learned; IQL [24] and MAPPO [27] are earlier published learned beam-hopping schemes compared on throughput (Figs. 8-9).
q4_support: p. 9: "training complexity of the MFMAPPO algorithm used can be" O(T n^2), with O(K^2 N) planning, O(n) inference and O(K^3 log(1/xi)) power; Table II (p. 11) gives runtime 977 us for the proposed scheme.
q5_support: p. 10: "The simulation employs a timeslot" duration of 10 ms in the authors own simulator with Poisson traffic; no code or data link and no availability statement appear anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area and function: the paper frames the work as anti-jamming beam hopping, and anti-jamming is an excluded function, but the learned decision is the beam-to-cell allocation of a satellite link scored by throughput, with jamming only an interference term in the SINR (p. 4), so area 6 chosen; reviewer to confirm. q1: the link gain is built from ITU-R S.1528, S.465-6 and P.1853 plus Friis free-space loss in a custom simulator; marked met as another standardized model, reviewer to confirm that ITU-R recommendations count. q2: training and testing conditions are not separated in the text, so 0. q3: MFMAPPO is a variant of the proposed method and does not count, IQL and MAPPO do.
